title: Role of Interfacial Coherency on Creep Behavior of FCC/BCC High-Entropy Alloy Multilayers.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: FCC/BCC high-entropy alloy multilayers, likely fabricated from elements such as Ni, Co, Fe, Cr, Mn (FCC) and perhaps Fe, Cr, Mo, Nb (BCC)
recollection.intervention: Guess: Variation of interfacial coherency between FCC and BCC layers, possibly by tuning composition or deposition conditions
recollection.structure: Guess: Alternating nanoscale multilayers of FCC and BCC high-entropy alloys with varying degrees of lattice coherency at interfaces
recollection.mechanism: Guess: Interfacial coherency affects dislocation transmission and creep resistance, with coherent interfaces impeding dislocation motion and enhancing creep strength
recollection.results: Guess: Quantitative results likely show that multilayers with higher interfacial coherency exhibit improved creep resistance, possibly measured as lower creep rates or higher activation energies compared to incoherent interfaces

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies varying FCC/BCC interfacial coherency and a nanoscale multilayer structure. It misses the specific 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm modulation periods and their coherent, semicoherent, or grain-boundary-dominated structures. Its mechanism is materially wrong: the semicoherent M16 interfaces, not the fully coherent interfaces, provided the greatest creep resistance through dislocation pileup and proposed interfacial amorphization/diffusion or interface slip. No numerical creep displacements, rates, or stress exponents are recalled.
